name: Sonnet contrarian turnarounds
strategy: Fade H1's extremes: buy the AI-disruption-fear and macro-beaten-down names with real turnaround catalysts (ADBE/CRM/PYPL, oversold crypto, small caps, gold), while trimming the most overextended momentum trade (SOXL) short.

positions.thesis: Holding flat at $265 (Hold consensus $269.61 PT, CLSA $300) even as MS cut to Underweight on AI-competition risk — bracket unchanged, letting the stop/TP manage the analyst split rather than adding into a name near fair value.
Turnaround confirming further: $1.6B VA contract, raised FY26 guidance, +3.2% on 8/7 to $192.74, 53 analysts at Buy with a $241.72 target (~25% upside) — adding on continued momentum.

Management says the turnaround is 'progressing' with raised profit guidance, and the board rejecting Stripe/Advent's $53B bid while staying 'open to higher offers' confirms real strategic value the market was missing — sizing up on genuine takeover-premium optionality, adding a stop for the first time given single-name/deal-binary risk.
Bounce continuing (+3.1% over 7 days) on sustained ETF inflows and whale accumulation — modest add, thesis intact but not yet dramatic.
ETF inflows accelerating (+$245M weekly) plus rising stablecoin activity on-chain support the laggard-to-leader turnaround — modest add.

Small caps still running (+1.11% on 8/7) on rate-cut hopes, but Wells Fargo flags deteriorating earnings estimates behind the price gains — holding small size with a protective stop rather than chasing.

The contrarian catalyst finally materialized: weak August jobs data drove gold to 7-week highs near $4,350 (+2.26% on 8/7) on rate-cut/dollar-weakness expectations — sizing back up from last week's watch-size trim.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-08: Closing the SOXL short: it moved from $114.72 (7/31 entry) to $140.25 (8/7 close), a +22.3% adverse move against the short and only ~2.3% from the -25% stop. A weak August jobs report on 8/7 triggered a broad rate-cut/dollar-weakness rally that lifted gold, semis and small caps simultaneously — not a one-day short-covering blip: 'Semiconductor Outlook Bodes Well for This ETF' and an Elliott Wave bounce call both point to a real fundamental threat to the crash thesis, and the sister GDX short in my other book already got stopped out on 8/7 in the same complex. Taking the loss on my own terms now rather than risking a worse forced stop, and rotating the freed capital into turnaround longs that are still confirming (CRM contract win + raised guidance, PYPL takeover optionality) plus gold, whose contrarian catalyst has finally shown up.
research_notes:
Read the account packet (Round 2 NAV $1,022.13/+2.21%; Round 3 NAV $948.01/-5.20%, GDX short already stopped out 8/7 @ $89.89). Pulled live/current data via WebFetch (stockanalysis.com, coingecko) since WebSearch budget was exhausted:

Key finding: a weak August 2026 jobs report hit on/around 8/7, driving rate-cut expectations and a dollar-weakness/risk-on rally that lifted gold, leveraged semis, small caps AND consumer discretionary simultaneously — this explains why gold miners (GDX) and leveraged semis (SOXL) both squeezed violently in the same week the task flagged (GDX stopped out 8/7 @ $89.89 vs ~$74.10 7/31 entry, +21%; SOXL 7/31 entry $114.72 -> 8/7 close $140.25, +22.3% adverse, only ~2.3% from its -25% stop in both books). News flow (Barron's 'Jacked-Up Tech ETF Demands a Strong Stomach', 'Semiconductor Outlook Bodes Well', an Elliott Wave bounce call, and gold at 7-week highs near $4,350 on weak jobs data) suggests this has real macro legs, not pure short-covering noise — so I closed SOXL preemptively in both books rather than wait for a second forced stop in the same complex that has already eaten 12 of 17 fired standing orders in this experiment.

Checked and confirmed still-working longs: ADBE $265.21 (Hold, MS cut to UW on AI-competition risk vs CLSA $300 PT — flat sizing), CRM $192.74 (+3.2% on 8/7, $1.6B VA contract, raised FY26 guidance, Buy consensus $241.72 PT — added), PYPL $59.07 (Stripe/Advent's $53B bid rejected, board 'still open to higher offers,' raised profit guidance — added with a first-time stop), IWM $301.56 (+1.11% but Wells Fargo flags weakening earnings estimates behind the rally — held small with a new stop), GLD $398.47 (+2.26% on 8/7, 7-week highs — the contrarian catalyst flagged at inception finally showed up, sized back up), BTC ~+3.1%/7d and ETH ~+2.9%/7d (bounce continuing on ETF inflows, modest adds).

Round 3 sector breakouts all still confirming: KRE (+31.5%/1yr, 'cheaper way to play the AI banking boom'), XLV (+0.75% on 8/7, State Street upgraded healthcare to positive for Q3), XBI (+1.86% on 8/7, M&A and trial catalysts) — added to all three with the capital freed by closing SOXL. Trimmed the XLY short leg of the utilities/discretionary pair (XLY +1.49% on 8/7 vs XLU +0.53%, discretionary being lifted by the same risk-on move) rather than eliminating it, and raised cash meaningfully in Round 3 (13% -> 29%) given the book's -7.51% max drawdown and the whipsaw risk still evident in the short-book complex.

Overlap check: closing SOXL in both books (previously short 20% in each — the only shared symbol) drops same-direction gross-weight overlap between Round 2 and Round 3 to zero, comfortably under the <50% requirement.
